category: debrid resale - lifetime deal sold through a bundle marketplace

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable to the resale: the single-object cap is the debrid vendor's, not the shop's

retention.stated: not applicable to the resale: cached-item retention is the debrid vendor's

interface_detail: the shop delivers a voucher code or a login by email; the capacity itself is reached through the debrid vendor's REST API
tooling: any client that takes the vendor's API key: rclone, JDownloader, Stremio/Torrentio, pyload
chaining: a resold voucher only changes how the days are paid for; the stack above it is unchanged
confidence_note: the seller's page was read; a seller is not the vendor, so nothing here is at the documented rung except the vendor terms quoted in evidence

free_tier.stated: One-off 'lifetime' purchase: US$39.99 and later US$36.19 through StackSocial, and EUR 29.25 on a German deal run posted 2025-09-21 and expired 2025-11-17. PCWorld's shop still lists it as 'Offcloud Lifetime Subscription' with 'Length of access: lifetime'.
free_tier.notes: the seller is a deal marketplace; the service is Offcloud, which still sells a yearly plan at EUR 40

egress.terms: the lifetime SKU's own specs: 'Unlimited remote uploads', '50GB of cloud space', '30GB of monthly quota for premium sources'. The monthly 30 GB is the real ceiling behind the word unlimited.

limits.value: lifetime converted to a one-year membership in January 2026

identity_cost.detail: marketplace account plus an Offcloud account; no identity document

reliability_note: Buyers report the lifetime was replaced: 'I purchased this service during their last Lifetime StackSocial sale in October 2025. Today in January 2026, they claim that a member of staff passed and they are changing everything' (2026-01-24); 'given a 1 year free premium. Now my account instead of being a lifetime premium' (2026-02-18). A Taiwanese buyer got the same answer from support on 2026-01-21: the old lifetime is invalid and the compensation is one year. Trustpilot's aggregate is 1.8/5 from 86 reviews.

evidence.proved: 'Length of access: lifetime', 'Max number of device(s): 3 IP addresses', '50GB of cloud space', '30GB of monthly quota for premium sources'
the 1.8/5 score from 86 reviews and two dated reports (2026-01-24, 2026-02-18) that lifetime buyers were moved to a one-year or yearly plan
2026-01-21 buyer post plus the same-day follow-up quoting support: the new team runs it, the old lifetime is invalid, the compensation is one year
the US$36.19 StackSocial run, now marked expired and posted about a year before 2026-10-23
the last run: '29,25€', posted 2025-09-21, 'Dieser Deal ist abgelaufen am 17. Nov. 2025'

notes: The clearest dated death: a lifetime debrid bought in October 2025 was converted in January 2026. The vendor did not close, which is worse for the buyer than a closure: the service continues on a plan the buyer did not choose, and Offcloud's terms state no refund is available. Even while it was sold, the 'unlimited' lifetime carried a 30 GB/month premium-source quota. Recorded as the offer's verdict; Offcloud's yearly plan is priced in pricing-history/records/offcloud.json and is not re-recorded here.
